learning_objective: 🎯 Let us explore how heavy solid things are and how much liquid different containers can hold!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: We measure light things like a pencil in Grams (g). For heavy things like a big sack of potatoes or your own body weight, we use Kilograms (kg)!
Capacity tells us how much liquid a container can hold. We use Milliliters (ml) for small drops of medicine and Liters (L) for big buckets of water.
If you pour water from a 1 Liter bottle into small cups, you will see that it takes many small cups to empty the big bottle. The total amount of water stays the same!

fun_activity.title: 🥛 Kitchen Capacity Hunt
fun_activity.instructions: Go to your kitchen safely with an elder. Look at a milk packet or a water bottle and find where 'ml' or 'L' is written. Write down the numbers!

quick_recap: ⭐ We use Grams (g) and Kilograms (kg) to check how heavy solid objects are.
⭐ We use Milliliters (ml) and Liters (L) to measure liquids like water and milk.
⭐ A bigger container has more capacity than a smaller container.
